newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn wants early deal on Holocaust compensation.
newsitem.headline: Bonn wants early deal on Holocaust compensation.

text.p: Germany said on Wednesday it wanted to reach an early accord on compensation to thousands of Jewish Holocaust survivors in the former eastern bloc.
"The government will be seeking to reach quick agreement after the summer recess (of parliament)," government spokesman Herbert Schmuelling told reporters.
Schmuelling said Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl and representatives of the finance ministry would meet a delegation from the Jewish Claims Conference next week for talks on the matter.

Germany has been under increasing pressure to resolve a long-running dispute over compensation to Holocaust victims in eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union, who during the Cold War were excluded from reparations made to western victims.
The Claims Conference and other Jewish groups are demanding that anything between 15,000 and 40,000 eastern European Holocaust survivors should be made eligible for German pensions.

Bonn has said around 1.5 billion marks ($804 million) has been set aside for Holocaust survivors in Poland, Russia, Ukraine and Belarus but campaigners complain that some victims have received no payments at all. ($ = 1.865 German Marks)
